_note: Draft English rendering of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Devarim 28, generated by scripts/translate_tafsir_english.py against the JA (not the biblical Hebrew). Translation goal: reverse-translatability for the Tafsir reader — readers should be able to map English back to JA. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: And know that if you hear and obey the command of God your Lord, to keep and to do all His commandments which I command you today, God your Lord shall set you high above all the rest of the nations of the earth.
translations.2: All these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you, since you have heard the command of God your Lord.
translations.3: And you shall be blessed in the settlement, and blessed in the open wilderness.
translations.4: Blessed shall be the fruit of your body, and the fruit of your gardens, and the fruit of your beasts — the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flocks.
translations.5: And blessed shall be what is in your panniers and your kneading-troughs.
translations.6: And you shall be blessed in your entering, and blessed in your going out.
translations.7: And God shall make your enemies who rise up against you to be stricken before you; by one road they shall come out against you, and by seven roads they shall flee from before you.
translations.8: And God shall command His blessing upon you — in your granaries, and in all the work of your hand; and He shall bless you in the land which God your Lord is giving you.
translations.9: And God shall establish you for Himself as a holy people, as He promised you, when you keep His commandments and walk in His ways.
translations.10: And all the nations of the earth shall see that the name of God has been called upon you, and they shall fear you.
translations.11: And God shall increase your good — in the fruit of your body, and the fruit of your beasts, and the fruit of your gardens — in the land which He swore to your fathers that He would give you.
translations.12: And God shall open for you His good treasuries from the sky, to send down the rain of your land in its season, and to bless you in all the work of your hand; so that you shall lend to many nations, and you shall not borrow.
translations.13: And God shall make you a head and not a tail, and you shall be only on top and not be brought low — when you accept the commandments of God your Lord which I command you today, to keep them and to do by them.
translations.14: And do not deviate from any of the things which I command you today, right or left, so as to follow other objects of worship and serve them.
translations.15: But if you do not accept the command of God your Lord, to keep and to do all His commandments and statutes which I command you today, then all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you.
translations.16: And you shall be cursed in the settlement, and cursed in the open wilderness.
translations.17: And cursed shall be what is in your panniers and your kneading-troughs.
translations.18: And cursed shall be the fruit of your body and the fruit of your land, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flocks.
translations.19: And you shall be cursed in your entering, and cursed in your going out.
translations.20: And God shall send upon you ruin and confusion and rebuke, in all the work of your hand that you do — until your destruction and your swift annihilation; and they shall say: because of the evil of your ways, in that you have forsaken Me.
translations.21: And God shall fasten upon you the pestilence, until He has consumed you from the land which you are entering to possess.
translations.22: And God shall strike you with the fever of consumption and with burning heat, and with quartan fever and with palsy, and with drought and with scorching wind and with jaundice — they shall pursue you until your destruction.
translations.23: And your sky which is above your head shall be like copper, and the earth which is beneath you like iron.
translations.24: And God shall make the water of His rain upon your land into dust and earth — from the sky it shall scatter down upon you, until your destruction.
translations.25: And God shall make you to be stricken before your enemies; by one road you shall go out against them, and by seven roads you shall flee from before them — and you shall become a lesson to all the kingdoms of the earth.
translations.26: And your corpse shall become food for the bird of the sky and the beasts of the earth, with none to frighten them away.
translations.27: And God shall strike you with the boil of Egypt, and with hemorrhoids, and with scab and with itch — which you shall not be able to cure.
translations.28: And God shall strike you with madness and with blindness and with bewilderment of heart.
translations.29: So that you shall grope about like one feeling his way at noon, as the blind man gropes, and especially in darkness; and your ways shall not prosper; and you shall be only oppressed and plundered all the time, with no one to save you.
translations.30: If you marry a woman, another man shall come to her; and you shall build a house but not dwell in it; and you shall plant a vineyard but not use its fruit.
translations.31: And your ox shall be slaughtered before your eyes, and you shall not eat of it; and your donkey shall be plundered from before you and shall not return to you; and your flock shall be given over to your enemies, with no one to save you.
translations.32: Your sons and your daughters shall be handed over to another people, and your eyes shall see them, staring toward them all the time, with no power in your hand.
translations.33: And the fruit of your land and the rest of your earnings shall be eaten by a people you do not know; and you shall be thus — oppressed and crushed all the time.
translations.34: Until you become demented from the sight of your eyes that you see.
translations.35: And God shall strike you with a malignant boil on the knees and on the legs, which you shall not be able to cure — and that which pains you from your foot to the crown of your head.
translations.36: And God shall exile you, and your king whom you shall set over you, to a people whom neither you nor your fathers have known; and there you shall serve other objects of worship of wood and stone.
translations.37: And you shall become a desolation, a byword and a tale, among all the nations to which God shall drive you.
translations.38: When the open land brings forth much seed, little shall you gather from it — for the locusts shall devour it.
translations.39: If you plant a vineyard and till it, you shall not drink wine from it nor store it — for the worm shall eat it.
translations.40: If you have olive trees throughout all your territory, you shall not anoint yourself with the oil — for it shall scatter its fruit.
translations.41: And if you beget sons or daughters, they shall not remain yours — for they shall go into captivity.
translations.42: And all your trees and the fruit of your land the locust shall gnaw away.
translations.43: The stranger who is among you shall rise above you higher and higher, while you shall sink lower and lower.
translations.44: Until he shall lend to you, and you shall not lend to him; he shall become a head and you shall become a tail.
translations.45: And all these curses shall come upon you, and pursue you, and overtake you — until your destruction — since you did not accept the command of God your Lord, and keep His commandments and His statutes which I command you.
translations.46: And they shall be among you a sign and a proof — and among your offspring who resemble you — forever.
translations.47: In return for the fact that you did not serve God your Lord with joy and goodness of heart, out of the abundance of all things —
translations.48: you shall therefore serve your enemy whom God shall set over you, in hunger and in thirst, and in nakedness and in want of everything; and he shall place a yoke of iron upon your neck, until he has destroyed you.
translations.49: And God shall send against you a nation from afar, from the end of the earth — as the eagle circles — a nation whose language you shall not understand.
translations.50: A brazen nation, which shall show no favor to the old, and shall not have compassion on the young.
translations.51: And it shall eat the fruit of your beasts and the fruit of your land until your destruction, leaving you no grain, no juice, and no oil, and no offspring of your cattle and young of your flocks — until it has annihilated you.
translations.52: And it shall besiege you in all your quarters, until it has broken down your high and fortified walls in which you trust throughout all your land; and it shall press you hard in all your quarters throughout all the land which God your Lord has given you.
translations.53: Until you eat the fruit of your womb — the flesh of your sons and your daughters — which God your Lord has provided for you — in the siege and the distress with which your enemy shall besiege you.
translations.54: So that even the most tender and delicate man among you shall begrudge his brother, and the wife of his bosom, and the rest of his children whom he has left surviving —
translations.55: from giving any of them of the flesh of his children that he eats, since nothing has been left to him — in the siege and the distress with which your enemy shall press you hard in all your quarters.
translations.56: So that even the most tender and delicate woman among you, who has never accustomed her foot to be set upon the ground, out of delicacy and tenderness, shall begrudge her husband, and her son and her daughter —
translations.57: and her afterbirth that falls from her, and the infants she delivers — so that she hoards them to herself and eats them, out of want of everything, in secret — in the siege and the distress with which your enemy shall press you hard in your quarters.
translations.58: And if you do not keep and do all the words of this Torah written in this book, and do not fear this noble and awe-inspiring Name — He is God your Lord —
translations.59: then God shall make your plagues wondrous, and the plagues of your offspring aforementioned: great and harmful plagues, and malignant harmful diseases.
translations.60: And He shall bring back upon you all the ailments of Egypt which you dreaded — and they shall cling to you.
translations.61: Also every disease and every plague that is not written in the book of this Torah, God shall set them over you until He has destroyed you.
translations.62: And you shall be left a numbered band, after you had been as the stars of the sky in multitude — since you did not accept the command of God your Lord.
translations.63: And it shall be: just as God intended for you to deal well with you and to multiply you, so shall He intend for you to destroy you and to annihilate you; and you shall be obliterated from the land which you are entering to possess.
translations.64: And God shall scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other; and there you shall serve other objects of worship which neither you nor your fathers have known — of wood and stone.
translations.65: And among those nations you shall find no rest, and there shall be no resting-place for your foot; but God shall give you there a trembling heart, and staring eyes, and withering of soul.
translations.66: And your life shall be hanging before you, and you shall be terrified night and day, and shall not trust in your life.
translations.67: In the morning you shall say: 'Would that it were evening!' and in the evening you shall say: 'Would that it were morning!' — out of the dread of your heart which you shall dread, and from the sight of your eyes which you shall see.
translations.68: And God shall bring you back to the condition of Egypt in ships — along the way of which I said to you: you shall never see it again — and you shall be offered there for sale to your enemies as slaves and maidservants, with no buyer.
translations.69: These are the words of the covenant which God commanded Moses to make with the sons of Israel in the land of Moab — apart from the covenant which He made with them at Mount Horeb.
